origin.description: There are two kinds of locks, exclusive and shared, see the exclusive argument and other details below.
origin.usage:
lock(path, exclusive = TRUE, timeout = Inf)

unlock(lock)

arguments.name: path
arguments.text: Path to the file to lock. If the file does not exist, it will be created, but the directory of the file must exist. Do not place the lock on a file that you want to read from or write to.

arguments.name: exclusive
arguments.text: Whether to acquire an exclusive lock. A non-exclusive lock is a shared lock. Multiple processes can hold a shared lock on the same file.

arguments.name: timeout
arguments.text: Timeout to acquire the lock in milliseconds. Inf waits indefinitely. Zero returns immediately.

arguments.name: lock
arguments.text: The lock object to unlock. Unlocking an already unlocked lock is not an error. An unlocked lock cannot be locked again.

origin.details:
Always use special files for locking. Do not place the lock on a file you want to read or write. Create a special file, for example by appending .lock, and lock that. lock() creates the file when it does not exist. Reading or writing a locked file has undefined behavior.

All locks set by this package might be advisory. On Unix the lock is an fcntl record lock kept on an open descriptor. A second handle in the same process shares that descriptor. Closing any descriptor for the file releases every lock this process holds on it.

unlock() drops one handle. The kernel lock remains until the last handle is released. Releasing an already unlocked handle returns true.
origin.value: lock returns a filelock_lock object, or NULL when the wait times out. unlock returns TRUE.
origin.example:
mylockfile <- tempfile()
lck <- lock(mylockfile)
print(lck)
lock(mylockfile, timeout = 0)
lock(mylockfile, timeout = 5000)
lock(mylockfile, timeout = Inf)
